bottom_line: In patients with acute coronary syndromes with scheduled percutaneous coronary intervention, the primary efficacy end point occurred in 12.1% of patients receiving clopidogrel and 9.9% of patients receiving prasugrel (hazard ratio for prasugrel vs. clopidogrel, 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.90; P<0.001).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, prasugrel reduced the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke versus clopidogrel (9.9% vs. 12.1%; hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73–0.90) while increasing non–CABG-related TIMI major bleeding (2.4% vs. 1.8%; hazard ratio, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.03–1.68) and fatal bleeding (0.4% vs. 0.1%). It does not establish a significant difference in overall mortality because death from any cause was 188 (3.0) with prasugrel and 197 (3.2) with clopidogrel (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.78–1.16).

major_points.text: Randomized trial in ACS patients with scheduled PCI comparing prasugrel vs clopidogrel for 6 to 15 months with a specified loading and maintenance dose regimen.
major_points.quote: we randomly assigned 13,608 patients with moderate-to-high-risk acute coronary syndromes with scheduled percutaneous coronary intervention to receive prasugrel (a 60-mg loading dose and a 10-mg daily maintenance dose) or clopidogrel (a 300-mg loading dose and a 75-mg daily maintenance dose), for 6 to 15 months.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of the rate of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke during the follow-up period.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was lower with prasugrel than with clopidogrel in the overall cohort.
major_points.quote: In the overall cohort, a total of 781 patients (12.1%) in the clopidogrel group had the primary end point, as compared with 643 patients (9.9%) in the prasugrel group (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.90; P<0.001)

major_points.text: Stent thrombosis was reduced with prasugrel compared with clopidogrel.
Major bleeding (non–CABG-related TIMI major bleeding) was higher with prasugrel than with clopidogrel.
Fatal TIMI major bleeding occurred more often with prasugrel than with clopidogrel.

subgroups.text: Patients were randomly assigned in two strata: UA/NSTEMI and STEMI.
subgroups.quote: Patients were randomly assigned to the clopidogrel group or the prasugrel group in two strata: 10,074 pa- tients with moderate-to-high-risk unstable angi- na or non–ST-elevation myocardial infarction and 3534 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarc- tion.

subgroups.text: Major prespecified subgroups showed no significant interactions with treatment effect.
subgroups.quote: Prasugrel showed superior efficacy in major prespecified subgroups (Fig. 2), without signifi- cant interactions between the characteristics of the patients and the treatment group.

subgroups.text: Patients with a history of stroke or TIA had net harm from prasugrel (HR 1.54; P=0.04).
subgroups.quote: patients who had a previous stroke or transient ischemic at- tack had net harm from prasugrel (hazard ratio, 1.54; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.32; P = 0.04)

harms.text: Non–CABG-related TIMI major bleeding was higher with prasugrel than clopidogrel.
Fatal TIMI major bleeding occurred more often with prasugrel than clopidogrel.
More patients receiving prasugrel discontinued study drug due to adverse events related to hemorrhage.
harms.quote: More patients treated with prasugrel (2.5%, vs. 1.4% of patients treated with clopidogrel; P<0.001) discontinued the study drug owing to adverse events related to hemorrhage.

harms.text: Serious adverse events not related to hemorrhage were similar between groups.
harms.quote: The rate of serious adverse events not related to hemorrhage was similar in the prasugrel group and the clopidogrel group (occurring in 22.5% and 22.8% of patients, respectively; P = 0.52).

harms.text: Intracranial hemorrhage was reported in 0.3% in each group.
harms.quote: Intracranial hemorrhage was reported in 19 patients (0.3%) receiving prasu­ grel and 17 patients (0.3%) receiving clopidogrel (P = 0.74).

inclusion_criteria.text: Acute coronary syndromes with scheduled PCI.
inclusion_criteria.quote: We enrolled 13,608 patients with acute coronary syndromes (representative of the entire spectrum of those syndromes) with scheduled PCI.

inclusion_criteria.text: For unstable angina/NSTEMI: ischemic symptoms lasting 10 minutes or more within 72 hours before randomization.
inclusion_criteria.quote: The inclusion criteria for patients with un- stable angina or non–ST-elevation myocardial infarction were ischemic symptoms lasting 10 minutes or more and occurring within 72 hours before randomization

inclusion_criteria.text: For unstable angina/NSTEMI: TIMI risk score of 3 or more.
inclusion_criteria.quote: The inclusion criteria for patients with un- stable angina or non–ST-elevation myocardial infarction were ischemic symptoms lasting 10 minutes or more and occurring within 72 hours before randomization, a TIMI risk score19 of 3 or more

inclusion_criteria.text: For unstable angina/NSTEMI: either ST-segment deviation of 1 mm or more or elevated levels of a cardiac biomarker of necrosis.
inclusion_criteria.quote: a TIMI risk score19 of 3 or more, and either ST-segment deviation of 1 mm or more or elevated levels of a cardiac biomarker of necrosis.

inclusion_criteria.text: For STEMI: enrolled within 12 hours after symptom onset if primary PCI planned.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction could be enrolled within 12 hours after the onset of symptoms if primary PCI was planned

inclusion_criteria.text: For STEMI: enrolled within 14 days after receiving medical treatment for STEMI.
inclusion_criteria.quote: or within 14 days after receiving medical treat- ment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

Key exclusion criteria included an in- creased risk of bleeding, anemia, thrombocyto- penia, a history of pathologic intracranial findings

exclusion_criteria.text: Use of any thienopyridine within 5 days before enrollment.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Key exclusion criteria included an in- creased risk of bleeding, anemia, thrombocyto- penia, a history of pathologic intracranial findings, or the use of any thienopyridine within 5 days before enrollment.

analysis_methods.text: Gehan–Wilcoxon test for primary end point; log-rank for sensitivity and other analyses.
analysis_methods.quote: The Gehan–Wil- coxon test was used to compare the treatment groups with regard to the primary efficacy end point18; the log-rank test was used in a prespeci- fied sensitivity analysis for the primary end point

analysis_methods.text: Closed testing procedure: primary end point analyzed first in UA/NSTEMI cohort, then overall cohort only if significant.
analysis_methods.quote: we used a closed testing procedure. The primary efficacy end point was analyzed in the cohort with unstable angina or non–ST-elevation myocardial infarction first, and only if there was a statistically significant difference

analysis_methods.text: Planned 90% power to detect a 20% reduction in relative risk of the primary end point in UA/NSTEMI.
analysis_methods.quote: We calculated that a total of 875 primary end points would be required for the study to have a 90% power to detect a 20% reduction in the rela- tive risk of the primary end point
